questions.question: If the trailer drifts while you are backing, what should you do?

options.text: Return the steering wheel to the 12 o'clock position.
Turn the top of the steering wheel toward the drift.
Turn the top of the steering wheel away from the drift.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn the top of the steering wheel toward the drift.
questions.explanation: If your trailer drifts while backing, fix it right away. Turn the top of the steering wheel in the direction the trailer is drifting.

questions.question: What is the Johnson bar?

options.text: A hand valve that controls the trailer brakes
A valve that shows the fuel level
A valve that limits the amount of cargo

questions.correctAnswerText: A hand valve that controls the trailer brakes
questions.explanation: The Johnson bar is a hand valve used to control the trailer brakes. It should only be used to test the brakes. Using it while driving can cause the vehicle to skid.

questions.question: When uncoupling, the landing gear should be:
questions.explanation: When uncoupling, lower the landing gear until it makes firm contact with the ground. If the trailer is loaded, turn the crank a few extra times to remove some weight from the trailer.

questions.question: When coupling, you should:

options.text: Connect only one set of glad hands.

questions.explanation: Make sure you connect the correct pairs of glad hands when coupling air brake hoses. They are sometimes color-coded to help you avoid mistakes. Blue is usually for service lines and red is usually for emergency lines.

questions.question: In a double or triple combination, which trailer should be closest to the cab?
questions.explanation: Put the heaviest trailer closest to the tractor. Put the lightest trailer at the back.

questions.question: Why are roads especially slippery when rain first starts?

options.text: Fresh rain mixes with oil on the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fresh rain mixes with oil on the road.
questions.explanation: When rain first starts, it mixes with oil on the road that has not yet washed away. This creates a very slippery surface.

questions.question: When should you check and adjust your mirrors?
questions.explanation: Check and adjust your mirrors before you start driving. Your posture may change each day, so your mirrors may need adjustment.

questions.question: Is it safe to have ABS on only one axle?

options.text: Yes, it still gives you better control when braking.
Yes, but it only slows the vehicle, it cannot stop it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, it still gives you better control when braking.
questions.explanation: Even if ABS is on only the tractor, trailer, or one axle, you still have more braking control than without ABS. Brake normally.

questions.question: Mirror adjustment can only be checked properly if:

options.text: The vehicle is on a slight incline.

questions.explanation: With one or more trailers, you can only check mirror adjustment correctly if the trailers are straight. Check your mirrors before each trip.

questions.question: When entering traffic, a large vehicle needs:

options.text: About the same space as a car.

questions.explanation: Large vehicles need more space to enter or cross traffic than smaller vehicles. They are bigger and need a longer distance to accelerate.

questions.question: What gets removed when you drain an air tank?
questions.explanation: Air brake systems have drains that remove water and compressor oil from air tanks. If water and oil build up in the system, they can damage the brakes.

questions.question: What should you do to stay alert while driving?

options.text: Eat a heavy meal before your trip.
Drive with a second person who can take turns driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive with a second person who can take turns driving.
questions.explanation: Sharing driving duties with another driver reduces the risk that either driver will become tired. You can also stay alert by avoiding heavy meals and keeping the cab cool.

questions.question: How far does an air brake vehicle need to stop from 55 mph in ideal conditions?
questions.explanation: Stopping distance includes perception time, reaction time, brake lag, and actual braking distance. An air brake vehicle traveling at 55 mph needs about 450 feet to stop completely under ideal conditions.

questions.question: Which item is required emergency equipment?
questions.explanation: All commercial trucks must have emergency equipment. This includes spare electrical fuses, three reflective triangles or six fuses or three flares, and at least one fire extinguisher that is properly charged.

questions.question: What should you do when leaving your vehicle unattended?

options.text: Use the parking brake only when parked on a slope.
Do not use the parking brake because it damages tires.

questions.explanation: Always use the parking brake when you park. However, do not use it if your brakes are very hot or if they are wet and it is freezing.

questions.question: What should you do if your vehicle hydroplanes?

options.text: Turn the wheel as hard as possible.

questions.explanation: If your vehicle hydroplanes, do not brake. Instead, release the accelerator and push in the clutch to slow down. This helps you regain traction.

questions.question: What causes the "crack-the-whip" effect?
questions.explanation: Vehicles with trailers can roll over due to the "crack-the-whip" effect, which is caused by rearward amplification. Learn the rearward amplification of your specific vehicle.

questions.question: When can you rely on front wheel braking?
questions.explanation: Front wheel braking works well under all road conditions. Front wheels rarely skid, even on ice.

questions.question: A driver with an open window in cold weather may be:

options.text: Someone dressed wrong for the weather

questions.explanation: Watch other drivers for signs of impairment. Drivers who are drunk, tired, using drugs, or sick are dangerous. One warning sign is a driver with windows down in cold weather.

questions.question: What problem do vehicles behind a truck face?

options.text: They cannot see objects in front of the truck
They have a clear view of the road ahead
They do not need to signal

questions.correctAnswerText: They cannot see objects in front of the truck
questions.explanation: Your truck blocks the view of drivers behind you. They cannot see hazards ahead. Flash your brake lights and warn other drivers before you slow down or stop.
